nodes.label: ChainForge
nodes.rationale: Deliberately general-purpose, not built for a specific API or LLM back-end; ultimate goal is integration into other tools for systematic evaluation and auditing of LLMs. Focuses on evaluation across prompts, prompt parameters, and models, unlike the closed-source PromptChainer/AI Chains projects that inspired it.

nodes.label: Prompt Permutations (Combinatorial Cross Product)
nodes.rationale: Taking the cross product of inputs to prompt templates sends hundreds of queries at once, verifying model behavior more robustly than one-off prompting; templates can chain at arbitrary depth to compare templates themselves.

nodes.label: Model Settings Comparison
nodes.rationale: Multiple nicknamed copies of the same model with different settings let users measure e.g. the impact of a system message on ChatGPT.

nodes.label: Evaluation Nodes
nodes.rationale: Python-script-based probing of LLM responses; LLM responses can be chained into prompt templates to evaluate outputs cheaply before more extensive evaluation.

nodes.label: Visualization Nodes
nodes.rationale: Grouped box-and-whisker for numeric metrics and histograms for boolean metrics; only numeric and boolean metrics supported at time of writing.

nodes.label: Chat Turns Templating
nodes.rationale: Follow-up chat messages are templated just like prompts, enabling comparison of later responses across chat models or settings.

nodes.label: Flow Share Feature
nodes.rationale: To prevent abuse, only 10 flows may be shared at a time and each must be under 5MB compressed; oldest link breaks beyond 10, so users are told to export important flows to cforge files and use Share only ephemerally.

nodes.label: ChainForge Web Version (chainforge.ai/play)
nodes.rationale: Hosted version has a limited feature set; local install adds env-var API keys, Python code evaluation, and locally-run Ollama models.

nodes.label: Supported LLM Providers
nodes.rationale: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, HuggingFace, Together.ai, Ollama, Azure OpenAI, Aleph Alpha, Amazon Bedrock, plus arbitrary providers via custom provider scripts.

nodes.label: OpenAI Evals Registry
nodes.rationale: Source of 188 example evaluation flows shipped with ChainForge.

nodes.label: ChainForge CHI 2024 Paper (Arawjo et al.)
nodes.author: Arawjo, Ian and Swoopes, Chelse and Vaithilingam, Priyan and Wattenberg, Martin and Glassman, Elena L

nodes.label: chainforge Python Package (Flask server + CLI)
nodes.rationale: Entry point chainforge = chainforge.app:main; chainforge serve runs flask_app.py on port 8000.

nodes.label: react-server React/TypeScript Frontend
nodes.rationale: Create React App via craco; almost all application logic lives here. npm start/build/test scripts are gated by prettier+eslint; bypass with npx craco start for fast iteration.

nodes.label: In-Browser TypeScript Backend (src/backend/)
nodes.rationale: Full TypeScript reimplementation of ChainForge's core that executes client-side: LLM querying, prompt templating/permutation, response caching, model registry, shared types. This is why craco.config.js polyfills Node built-ins (buffer, crypto, stream, http, net) - browser code calls APIs that assume Node.

nodes.label: Thin Flask Backend (flask_app.py)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately thin: serves the built React app and only covers work that genuinely needs a server - /app/executepy Python eval subprocess, example/OpenAI-eval flows, env API keys, custom providers, flow storage, media upload, CORS image proxy.

nodes.label: Pyodide In-Browser Python Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Alternative to the Flask /app/executepy route: Python evaluation can run fully in-browser via src/backend/pyodide/, removing the server dependency.

nodes.label: FLASK_BASE_URL Frontend-Flask Wiring
nodes.rationale: FLASK_BASE_URL is '/' when served by Flask (detected via injected window.__CF_PORT), otherwise defaults to http://localhost:8000/. During frontend dev on port 3000, server-dependent features require a parallel Flask instance on 8000; pure in-browser features work with the dev server alone.

nodes.label: ReactFlow Node Graph (src/*Node.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Each src/*Node.tsx is a ReactFlow node type registered in the nodeTypes map in App.tsx; nodes read upstream inputs via pullInputData and write outputs to node.data.fields. data.fields is only an array on prompt/chat nodes - guard with Array.isArray elsewhere.

nodes.label: Zustand Store (store.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Holds nodes, edges, and initLLMProviderMenu (the model list shown in the UI).

nodes.label: Duplicated Model Registry (models.ts + store.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Adding or changing a model touches two places that must stay in sync: the NativeLLM enum plus rate-limit/cost tables in src/backend/models.ts, and initLLMProviderMenu in store.tsx. base_model selects which settings form in ModelSettingSchemas.tsx and must be unique per settings schema.

nodes.label: Validate Install CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Matrix-installs the package across 5 OSes and Python 3.11-3.13 with fail-fast disabled; running the server and pytest are still TODO, so CI only validates installability.

nodes.label: Preconverted OpenAI Evals Flows
nodes.rationale: Flows derived from a subset of OpenAI's evals registry are NOT bundled in the PyPI package but fetched from GitHub on demand, to avoid forcing users to install OpenAI evals (Git LFS, Python 3.9+, many dependencies). OpenAI evals itself is MIT-licensed (Copyright 2023 OpenAI).

nodes.label: React App HTML Shell (index.html)
nodes.rationale: CRA template with root div; favicon logo from bqlqn @ flaticon.com used with attribution.

nodes.label: evalgen: Grading and Evaluation Function Selection Module
nodes.author: Shreya Shankar
nodes.rationale: Takes a developer's prompt and examples, suggests evaluation criteria with developer confirmation, generates and evaluates multiple functions per criterion, and returns the function per criterion most aligned with the developer's grades - i.e., eval functions are selected by alignment with human judgment rather than generated blindly.
nodes.norm_label: evalgen: grading and evaluation function selection module

nodes.label: evalgen Executor Component
nodes.rationale: Main logic: background process generates and evaluates functions per criterion, updating each example's grading priority as function results stream in; exposes methods to query the next example to grade, set grades, and query the best function per criterion.

nodes.label: evalgen Utils Component
nodes.rationale: Types and prompts for criteria generation, function generation, and function execution.

nodes.label: evalgen OAI Utils Component
nodes.rationale: Utilities for interacting with the OpenAI API.
